speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are here to discuss a skin condition; can you describe the specific lesion, including its size, color, and any changes in shape or symptoms like bleeding or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The clinical presentation of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penis and finger in a 62-year-old heavy smoker from an endemic region is highly suspicious for SCC. Immediate biopsy of both lesions is required for histopathological confirmation.
